label: Scheme agent
summary: Each character who fills an agent slot in the scheme.
details: Agents are the characters filling the scheme's agent slots. Empty slots are skipped, because only characters are listed. Vanilla often uses it to collect the agents into a list or to pick the best one with ordered_ and order_by (for example by intrigue).

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only agents for which these conditions hold are used.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Sorts the agents (ordered_ form only).
fields.values: a script value, for example intrigue

label: Scheme agent slot
summary: Each agent slot of the scheme, whether someone fills it or not.
details: A slot is a place for one agent. Vanilla checks is_filled to find free slots, is_agent_slot_type to find a certain role (such as agent_thief), and uses slot_character to reach whoever sits in it. It removes slots with remove_agent_slot on the scheme.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only slots for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Secret
summary: Each secret the character has.
details: These are the secrets the character is hiding, such as a lover or a murder. You can narrow it to one kind of secret with type. Vanilla uses it to reveal or expose secrets, remove them, and to find secrets that suit a spymaster task.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Only secrets of this kind.
fields.values: a secret type, for example secret_lover

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only secrets for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Secret knower
summary: Each character who knows the secret.
details: Vanilla uses it to send an event to every knower except two named characters (in its marriage events), or to check whether a certain character is among them.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only knowers for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Secret participant
summary: Each character who is a participant in the secret.
details: The game's documentation only calls them participants in a secret. The secret knower list is a separate list. Vanilla only uses it in checks, to see whether a given character is among them.

label: Sibling
summary: Each brother or sister of the character.
details: Vanilla often writes even_if_dead = yes to include siblings who have died. Vanilla uses the list to find rivals, twins and candidates for a role, and to hand out opinions or events.

fields.name: even_if_dead
fields.text: Also include siblings who have died (vanilla writes it with yes).

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only siblings for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Side commander
summary: Each commander of every army on one side of a battle.
details: This is wider than the single character leading the battle: it covers the commander of every army on that side. Vanilla uses it to give commanders experience and glory.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only commanders for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Side knight
summary: Each knight fighting on one side of a battle.
details: Vanilla uses it to give knights prestige, raise their prowess, record battle history, or to pick one enemy knight at random.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only knights for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Side participant
summary: Each character who takes part in one side of a battle.
details: Vanilla uses it to give prestige or stress to everyone on a side, or to check things about them, such as whether one of them is a ruler.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only participants for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Situation county
summary: Each county involved in the situation.
details: A situation is a larger ongoing event; vanilla's uses are mostly natural disasters. Vanilla uses it to lower county control, remove county modifiers, or look at the holder and empire of an affected county.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only counties for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Group participant
summary: Each character who belongs to a participant group of a situation.
details: Runs from a participant group, not from the situation itself. Vanilla uses it a lot to send events to every member of a group, and to check things like modifiers on them.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only characters for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Situation participant
summary: Each character who takes part in the situation.
details: This covers the whole situation. To look at one region only, use the sub-region participant list. Vanilla uses it to send events, to start follow-up contracts with a chance, and to compare characters.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only characters for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Sub-region
summary: Each sub-region of the situation.
details: A situation can be split into sub-regions, each with its own phase. Vanilla uses it to change phases, trigger catalysts, and to check which phase a region is in or whether it holds a given county.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only sub-regions for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Sub-region county
summary: Each county in one sub-region of a situation.
details: The game warns that this list is not fast, so avoid running it often. Vanilla uses it to add or remove county modifiers and to find counties whose ruler is affected.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only counties for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Sub-region geographical region
summary: Each geographical region that belongs to one sub-region of a situation.
details: Vanilla only saves one of them as a scope with random_. The other forms are not used there.

label: Sub-region participant
summary: Each character who takes part in the situation within one sub-region.
details: Like the situation participant list, but only for characters in that sub-region. Vanilla uses it in debug events and to test whether a given character is among them.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only characters for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Sub-region participant group
summary: Each participant group of one sub-region of a situation.
details: Vanilla gives groups a type (for example nomad_rulers_capital) and checks whether a character is in one. It goes on from a group to its characters with the group participant list.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only groups for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Special building province
summary: Each province that has a slot for a special building, whether the building is built or not.
details: It works without a starting object, over the whole map. Vanilla uses it to pick a random such province, or to check for one that is close and has a special building.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only provinces for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Special guest
summary: Each special guest of the activity.
details: The game's documentation does not say how special guests differ from other guests. Vanilla only picks one at random to save it, or checks a modifier on them.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only guests for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Sponsored inspiration
summary: Each inspiration the character sponsors.
details: Each inspiration has an inspiration_owner, which vanilla reads. Vanilla uses the list to find a sponsored inspiration of a certain type, to look at where its owner is, or to advance its progress.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only inspirations for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Spouse
summary: Each spouse of the character.
details: Vanilla uses it constantly, for example to pick the spouse with random_, to collect candidates, to give opinions, or to divorce.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only spouses for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Spouse candidate
summary: Each character that the game considers a possible spouse for the character.
details: The game warns that this is very slow and should not be done often. Vanilla does not use it, and the game's documentation does not say who counts as a candidate.

label: Spread province
summary: Each province the legend has spread into.
details: Vanilla only counts them, to check whether a legend has reached at least a given number of provinces (for example 100 or 300).

label: Stewardship councillor
summary: Each councillor of the character whose task is based on stewardship.
details: Vanilla only checks them, for example that at least one exists, or that all of them have a stewardship skill of 20 or more.

label: Sub-realm barony
summary: Each barony in the character's sub-realm.
details: Only titles that hold land, or that have de jure vassal titles (titles below them by the map's borders) holding land, are counted. Vanilla uses it to refill garrisons and levies in the barony's province, and to check holders and special building slots.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only baronies for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Sub-realm county
summary: Each county in the character's sub-realm.
details: Only titles that hold land, or that have de jure vassal titles (titles below them by the map's borders) holding land, are counted. Vanilla uses it very often, for example to change county control, add county modifiers, or test culture and faith.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only counties for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Sub-realm duchy
summary: Each duchy in the character's sub-realm.
details: Only titles that hold land, or that have de jure vassal titles (titles below them by the map's borders) holding land, are counted. Vanilla uses it rarely, in a few checks on the holder.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only duchies for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Sub-realm empire
summary: Each empire title in the character's sub-realm.
details: Only titles that hold land, or that have de jure vassal titles (titles below them by the map's borders) holding land, are counted. Vanilla uses it twice: once to sort empires, once to test whether an empire is one particular title.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only empires for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Sub-realm kingdom
summary: Each kingdom in the character's sub-realm.
details: Only titles that hold land, or that have de jure vassal titles (titles below them by the map's borders) holding land, are counted. Vanilla uses it rarely, for example to add kingdoms to a list.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only kingdoms for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Sub-realm title
summary: Each title of any tier in the character's sub-realm.
details: Only titles that hold land, or that have de jure vassal titles (titles below them by the map's borders) holding land, are counted. Use tier in a limit to keep only one rank, as vanilla does when it picks counties or duchies and above.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only titles for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Subject
summary: Each vassal and each tributary of the character.
details: Vanilla uses it to collect subjects who suit a religious task (spreading a personal tenet).

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only subjects for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Subordinate
summary: Each religious subordinate of the character.
details: The game warns that challengers (antipopes) count as subordinates of the top superior, so the list can include them. Vanilla uses it to give opinions and to pick preachers.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only subordinates for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Invested succession candidate
summary: Each candidate the character supports, as an investor, for any title.
details: The list may include people outside the investor's top realm, or candidates who are no longer valid for an appointment, so check before acting on them.

label: Invested succession title
summary: Each title that has candidates the character supports as an investor.
details: The list may include titles outside the investor's top realm, which cannot be appointed, and the supported candidates may already be dead.

label: Succession appointment investor
summary: Each character who has invested in a candidate for this title.
details: You name the candidate with candidate. You can also add a value comparison so only investors who put in at least that much are listed. Vanilla uses it to message investors, and to count them.

fields.name: candidate
fields.text: The candidate whose investors are listed.

fields.name: value
fields.text: Only investors whose investment matches this comparison.
fields.values: a comparison such as value > 100, or a script value

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only investors for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Target title
summary: Each title that the casus belli targets.
details: Vanilla uses it to sort the targeted titles by tier, to save one, and to check them.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only titles for which these conditions hold are used.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Sorts the titles (ordered_ form only).
fields.values: a script value, for example tier

label: Targeting faction
summary: Each faction that is aimed at the character.
details: These are factions whose target is this character. You can filter by faction type. Vanilla uses it to find a particular faction, look at its members and leader, or raise discontent.

fields.name: faction_type
fields.text: Only factions of this type.
fields.values: a faction type, for example independence_faction

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only factions for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Targeting scheme
summary: Each scheme that is aimed at the character.
details: These are schemes whose target is this character; each has an owner. Vanilla uses it to find a scheme by type or owner, check whether it is exposed, and look at its agents.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only schemes for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Targeting secret
summary: Each secret that has the character as its target.
details: These are secrets whose target is this character. That is a different list from the character's own secrets (the secret list). Vanilla uses it to check who owns or knows such a secret.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only secrets for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Task contract
summary: Each task contract that is available or already accepted.
details: It works over the whole game, without a starting object. You can filter by contract type. Vanilla only uses it in checks, by type or by where the contract takes place.

fields.name: task_contract_type
fields.text: Only contracts of this type.

label: Task contract type
summary: Each task contract type defined in the game.
details: It lists the types themselves, not contracts that exist right now. It works over the whole game. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Tax collector
summary: Each tax collector the character employs.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick a tax collector for steward events, to count them, and to go on to the vassals each one collects from.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only tax collectors for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Tax collector vassal
summary: Each vassal the character collects taxes from, as their tax collector.
details: The starting character is the tax collector, and the list gives the vassals they collect from. Vanilla uses it to give those vassals opinions, and to save one for an event.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only vassals for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Tax slot
summary: Each tax slot the character has.
details: A tax slot holds a tax collector and the vassals they collect from. Vanilla only uses it in checks: whether a slot has a collector, and whether its vassals include a ruler.

label: Tax slot vassal
summary: Each vassal assigned to the tax slot.
details: Vanilla uses it to give these vassals opinions or character modifiers, to pick one for an event, and to check them.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only vassals for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Tenet
summary: Each religious tenet defined in the game.
details: It lists the tenets themselves, over the whole game, not the tenets of one faith. Vanilla uses it to pick one tenet that fits a condition and save it.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only tenets for which these conditions hold are used.

label: This title or one above it
summary: The title itself and each title above it in its de jure chain.
details: De jure means by the map's own borders, not by who holds what. So a county gives itself, its duchy, kingdom and empire. Vanilla uses it to check whether a given title is in that chain, and to sort the chain by tier.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only titles for which these conditions hold are used.

label: Heir to the title
summary: Each character in the line of succession for the title.
details: It follows the order the title would pass in. Vanilla uses it to collect heirs, to give them opinions, and to test their dynasty or house.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Only heirs for which these conditions hold are used.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Sorts the heirs (ordered_ form only).

label: Title interested in location
summary: Each title that treats the county as an important location.
details: Starts from a county. The game's documentation does not say what makes a location important to a title, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Joined faction
summary: Each faction the title has joined.
details: Vanilla only checks the list, for example whether a given faction is among them.
